subject: Clarifying data custody and ops checklist — Dedicated vs Private deployment
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@finchem.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying data custody and ops checklist — Dedicated vs Private deployment

Hi Lydia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map the right deployment option for FinChem (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private VPC / On‑prem).

Recap from our side:
- You described two workload classes: prototype analytics (low-sensitivity) and production risk-scoring (sensitive PII + regulated financial attributes).
- Compliance bar for production: encryption of data at rest/in transit, customer-managed key option, and network-level tenancy isolation.

Open questions (can you confirm?):
1) Key management: do you require HSM-backed, customer-held keys (BYOK) for tokenization workflows, or is KMS with strict access controls sufficient?
2) Network topology: Is a Private VPC deployment mandatory for production (no internet egress from model hosts), or would Dedicated capacity with strict peering and dedicated subnets meet your security team?
3) Audit artifacts: can you share the top 3 audit items you need from our side (e.g., audit logs retention window, access log formats, SOC‑2 artifact samples)?

I attached the short checklist we mentioned (redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf) and a blank SOC2 questions workbook (finchem-soc2-questions.xlsx) — fill out the high-priority rows and we’ll convert into a technical statement for your security review.

Next steps I propose: Rishi to sketch attack surface differences (latency/ops tradeoffs) between Dedicated and Private; Tessa to capture ops runbook items for HSM integration. If you confirm the KMS/HSM requirement and VPC mandate, we’ll scope a Private deployment proposal + timeline.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachment(s): redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (overview), finchem-soc2-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@finchem.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finchem.com>, FinChem IT <it@finchem.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying data custody and ops checklist — Dedicated vs Private deployment

Kim — thank you for the clear summary. Short answers below — I included Oliver (head of infra) and our IT alias for the more tactical questions.

1) Key management: HSM-backed, customer-controlled keys are required for production risk-scoring. We can provide an HSM cluster (on-prem) or accept a cloud HSM if keys are in our KMS with strict separation.
2) Network topology: Private VPC or on‑prem are non-negotiable for production. Dedicated in a vendor VPC is acceptable for non-production/dev workloads only.
3) Audit artifacts: short list — (a) access logs with principal IDs and timestamps (90d retention), (b) network flow records for host-to-host egress, (c) proofs of key rotation and key usage logs.

Attached is a filled first pass of the SOC2 questions — row-level notes on the KMS/HSM requirement. We’ll follow up with Oliver on specific IP whitelisting and peering details.

—Lydia
Lydia Chen
VP, Product Risk & Compliance
FinChem

Attachment(s): finchem-soc2-questions.xlsx (filled)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@finchem.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying data custody and ops checklist — Dedicated vs Private deployment

Thanks Lydia — helpful and clear. A few technical notes for the team and for FinChem to consider when evaluating Dedicated vs Private:

- Private VPC (Redwood Private): we can deliver a customer-controlled VPC with no shared tenant hosts, integrated with customer KMS/HSM via standard KMIP or cloud HSM connectors. This satisfies the non-negotiable items you listed. Ops impact: longer lead time (3–6 weeks) for network setup and HSM integration; requires a short security runbook and proofing window.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity in Redwood-hosted environment): provides dedicated GPU pools but still within Redwood's control plane and shared host tenancy. We can restrict network egress and offer customer KMS wrapping in many cases, but it does not fully eliminate shared infrastructure assumptions (so may not meet the "no shared tenancy" requirement for production).

- Hybrid option: run production models in Private VPC/on‑prem while keeping lower-sensitivity workloads on Dedicated for cost efficiency.

From an SLO/cost perspective: Private VPC adds network ops and longer provisioning but buys you full tenancy isolation and KMS/HSM control. I’ll draft a short matrix for Lydia that highlights tradeoffs (isolation, lead time, ops overhead, estimated monthly cost delta).

Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick confirmations, Lydia — and thanks Rishi for the clear tradeoff summary. Finalizing next steps so everyone has visibility: 

1) FinChem to confirm whether you will provide an on‑prem HSM cluster or prefer cloud HSM integration (action: Lydia / Oliver — target 2026-08-26).
2) Rishi will send the tradeoff matrix and a rough cost delta by 2026-08-24.
3) Tessa will draft a proposed security runbook and required audit log formats for engineering to ingest (due 2026-08-27).
4) I’ll prepare a Private deployment statement of work (SOW) outline and timeline if you confirm HSM + VPC requirement (target to share 2026-08-28).

If any of these dates don’t work for FinChem, let me know and we’ll adjust. We’ll attach the work product to the HubSpot deal and loop in our legal team once the SOW outline is agreed.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
